CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

What this is

nixmass is a CRAN R package that models snow water equivalent (SWE) from daily snow depth (hs, meters) series. It offers process-based models (delta.snow, HS2SWE) and empirical regression models (jo09, pi16, st10, gu19). Docs site: https://haraldschellander.github.io/nixmass/ (built by pkgdown).

Commands

Run from the package root in R (devtools/testthat workflow; no Makefile):

devtools::document()                         # regenerate man/ and NAMESPACE from roxygen
devtools::load_all()                          # load package for interactive work
devtools::test()                              # run all tests
testthat::test_file("tests/testthat/test-swe.delta.snow.R")   # single test file
devtools::test(filter = "hs2swe")             # tests whose file name matches
devtools::check()                             # full R CMD check (CRAN-like)
spelling::spell_check_package()               # spelling (also run via tests/spelling.R)

Shell equivalents: R CMD build . && R CMD check --as-cran nixmass_*.tar.gz.

Architecture

  • nixmass() (R/nixmass.R) is the user-facing wrapper. It takes a data.frame with date and hs columns, dispatches to one or more model functions by name (delta.snow, delta.snow.dyn_rho_max, hs2swe, jo09, pi16, st10, gu19), and returns an S3 object of class nixmass — a list with swe (named list, one entry per model), date, hs. summary.nixmass and plot.nixmass (ggplot2-based; density = TRUE requires a single delta.snow model run with layers = TRUE) live in the same file. Model-specific required args (alt/region.jo09, snowclass.st10, region.gu19) are validated here.
  • Each model is its own exported function in its own file (swe.delta.snow, hs2swe, swe.jo09, swe.pi16, swe.st10, swe.gu19) and can be called directly. Adding a model means: new R/<model>.R, a branch in the nixmass() dispatch loop, the name in the model argument choices, and roxygen @export.
  • swe.delta.snow (R/swe.delta.snow.R) is the core and largest model. It is a layer-based simulation: new snow creates layers; helper closures defined inside the function (dry_compaction, assignH, drenchH, scaleH, rho_max_dyn) handle compaction, overburden, and melt. Parameters come from a defaults list merged with the user’s model_opts via utils::modifyList; defaults differ depending on dyn_rho_max (age-dependent maximum density, Werkgarner 2026 calibration). Note the function default is dyn_rho_max = TRUE, whereas nixmass(model = "delta.snow") passes FALSE. layers = TRUE returns per-layer h/swe/age matrices (rows = layers, sized to the max layer count of any single season). strict_mode controls checks for strictly regular dates and a series starting at zero.
  • R/swe.delta.snow.para.R is an experimental parallel/season-segmented variant (swe.delta.snow.para, with .delta_snow_core). It duplicates the delta.snow core logic and is excluded from the build via .Rbuildignore — it is not part of the shipped package. Keep model changes in swe.delta.snow.R in sync with it only if intended.
  • Package-wide imports are declared via roxygen tags at the top of R/nixmass.R; NAMESPACE and man/ are generated — do not edit by hand.
  • Example dataset hsdata (data/hsdata.RData, documented in R/nixmass.R) is used throughout examples and tests.

Conventions

  • Input validation errors use stop() with specific messages that tests match via expect_error(..., "<message>") — keep message text in sync with tests.
  • Performance matters (v1.4.0 vectorised the delta.snow inner loops and removed <<-); avoid reintroducing superassignment or per-layer loops.
  • Record user-visible changes in NEWS (plain-text format, nixmass vX.Y.Z (release date: ...) headers) and bump Version/Date in DESCRIPTION.
  • koi/ and .github/workflows/koi.yml are a cosmetic daily README GIF; the bot’s “koi: draw the day’s koi” commits are unrelated to package code.
